role.altitude: The forensic officer keeps searching scenes, lifting prints, processing items and sealing evidence; handwriting labels, scene logs and custody forms and searching the store for items shrink.
skills_to_grow: Registering every trace at the scene so labels and custody records follow from it
role.ambitious_version: An officer whose every trace can be followed from the scene to the courtroom without a handwritten form.

tasks.short: Plan the search with the case team, look for trace evidence such as fingerprints, hairs, fibers or shoe impressions using alternative light sources, mark and photograph the traces and record them in the scene log.

steps.what: Forensic officer plans the search with the case team
Forensic officer looks for trace evidence such as fingerprints, hairs, fibers or shoe impressions, using alternative light sources
Forensic officer marks and photographs the traces found
Forensic officer records each trace in the scene log: number, location and type

tasks.design: Searching for traces stays fully with the officer. A trace registration app on the forensic device gives each trace a number and links the photos taken of it, with time and position, so the scene log fills as the officer works and only the trace type and description are typed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trace numbers, photo numbers and locations were written on paper and matched later.
tasks.enabler_now: Trace registration apps that link photos to trace numbers.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a fibre under the light that others walk past.

reach.learn: Whether linked photos reduce questions about where a trace came from.

evidence.claim: Camera apps record time and position with each photo and can link it to an item number.
High-risk processing of police data needs a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: searching and recording traces; lifting and processing are separate tasks.
Input contract for s4: trace numbers created by the officer in the app and photos taken with the linked camera; the app is used at about 80% of scenes.
Planning, searching and photographing keep their full time.
research_questions: Are scene logs complete more often?

incremental.description: Forensic officer checks the trace-photo links before closing the scene.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: scenes with few traces; high: large scenes with many traces.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select surfaces, dust selected areas of the crime scene and lift latent fingerprints following preservation procedures, photograph prints before lifting, and label and record each lift.

steps.what: Forensic officer selects the surfaces to dust
Forensic officer dusts selected areas and lifts latent fingerprints, adhering to preservation procedures
Forensic officer photographs prints before lifting
Forensic officer labels each lift and records trace number, surface and location

tasks.design: Choosing surfaces, dusting, lifting and photographing stay fully with the officer. Each lift card gets a barcode label printed from the trace registration app with case and trace number, and scanning it links the lift to its photo and location, so the officer only notes the surface.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lift cards were labelled and logged by hand at the scene.
tasks.enabler_now: Portable label printers and trace registration apps.
tasks.still_hard: Surfaces where powder destroys the print.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the surface a hand must have touched.

reach.learn: Whether linked photos of the print in place help comparisons.

evidence.claim: Portable printers print barcode labels from a registration app.
Police data in daily tasks may be kept at most five years unless a case needs longer.

assumptions: Boundary: lifting prints at the scene; comparing them is outside.
Input contract for s4: trace numbers created in the trace registration app and labels printed by the portable printer; used at about 80% of scenes; the rest are labelled by hand.
Selecting, dusting, lifting and photographing keep their full time.

incremental.description: Forensic officer keeps the label printer stocked and charged.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few lifts per scene; high: burglary series with many lifts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the method, analyze and process evidence at scenes, during autopsies or in the laboratory with powders and chemicals while wearing protective equipment, photograph results and record methods and results.

steps.what: Forensic officer chooses the processing method for each item
Forensic officer analyzes and processes evidence with powders and chemicals, wearing protective equipment
Forensic officer photographs the results of processing
Forensic officer records methods and results in the trace registration

tasks.design: Processing stays fully with the officer. In the trace registration, methods are picked from the lab's method list with the reagent batch scanned, and result photos are linked by scanning the item's barcode, so only observations are typed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Methods, batches and photo numbers were written per item by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Trace registrations with method lists and barcode-linked photos.
tasks.still_hard: Items where one method rules out another.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the order of methods that keeps both prints and DNA.

reach.learn: Whether recorded reagent batches help explain odd results.

evidence.claim: Registration systems record methods from pick lists and link photos by barcode.
AI that assesses the reliability of evidence is high-risk; the design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: processing items; examining results in the lab is outside.
Input contract for s4: item barcodes from the scene registration, the lab's method list and reagent batch labels.
Choosing methods, processing and photographing keep their full time.
research_questions: Are processing records complete in court?

incremental.description: Forensic officer keeps the method list current with the lab.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few items with long processing; high: many small items each needing a record.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Package and seal evidence, label it and record custody, book it into the store with its location, retrieve and transfer items to the lab or court, and check the store for items due for disposal.

steps.what: Forensic officer packages and seals each evidence item
Forensic officer fills in the package label and chain-of-custody form by hand
Forensic officer stores evidence in the evidence store and records its location
Forensic officer retrieves evidence for the lab or court and records the transfer
Forensic officer checks the store for items due for return or disposal

tasks.design: Each package gets a barcode label printed from the trace registration, carrying case and item number, and scanning it starts the custody record. Booking into the store is a scan of the item and the shelf barcode; retrieving shows the shelf, and a transfer is a scan with the receiver's signature on a tablet. The store system lists items whose case decision allows return or disposal. Packaging and sealing stay manual, and no item leaves the store without a person scanning it out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Labels, custody forms and store locations were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Barcode labels, shelf scans and tablet signatures in evidence systems.
tasks.still_hard: Large or odd items that do not fit standard packaging.
tasks.human_edge: Sealing an item so its integrity is beyond doubt in court.
tasks.altitude: Much less form filling; handling evidence stays careful and manual.

reach.learn: Whether scan-based custody cuts lost items.

evidence.claim: Evidence systems track items by barcode with custody records and shelf locations.
Scan logs per officer could monitor staff and need works council consent if used that way.

assumptions: Boundary: from packaging to storage, transfer and disposal listing; disposal decisions are the prosecutor's.

Input contract for s2: item registrations made at the scene in the trace registration app and labels from the portable printer, at about 80% of scenes; the rest are labelled by hand; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: barcode labels on every shelf, put up once by store staff.
Input contract for s5: case decisions on return or disposal entered by the prosecutor's office in the case system.
Packaging and sealing keep their full time.
s3 is mostly storing evidence by hand in the evidence store and keeps its full time.
s4 is mostly fetching evidence and handing it over in person under chain of custody; it keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do items go missing less often?

already_counted.description: Forensic officer resolves scans that do not match the expected item or shelf.

incremental.description: Evidence store staff label shelves and keep shelf codes current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few items and a small store; high: many items per case and frequent transfers to the lab.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
